paragraphs: Stepwise Preference Optimization trains diffusion models using preference information from intermediate image-generation steps. It can improve image aesthetics at reduced computational cost, but its effectiveness does not fully explain how its training signals work. This paper studies those signals by interpreting the method as gradient guidance: directions that steer learning toward preferred outputs.

That interpretation exposes two problems. The method weights generation stages unevenly, giving later steps too little influence, and its gradient estimates contain substantial noise. These findings connect the behavior of the training objective to the reliability of the updates it produces, rather than explaining alignment only through image likelihoods.

The proposed GradSPO algorithm uses a simpler loss and a noise-reduction strategy informed by gradient variance to improve training stability. Evaluations on SD 1.5 and SDXL report stronger human preference results than leading baselines, alongside better aesthetics and semantic faithfulness. The contribution combines an explanation of an existing method with changes that improve its reported alignment performance.
neurips-2025-a-gradient-guidance-perspec.tldr: GradSPO uses a gradient-guidance analysis to improve the stability and human-preference alignment of diffusion-model training.

paragraphs: When analysts choose new questions after seeing earlier answers, repeatedly using the same data can produce overfitting. Differentially private analysis can provide generalization guarantees for such workflows, but earlier guarantees assume a fixed dataset. This paper extends the analysis to situations where more observations arrive over time.

The framework allows analysts to decide when to ask questions based on both previous interactions and the current amount of data. It also accommodates mechanisms and empirical accuracy bounds that change over time. This matters because an analysis should be able to obtain tighter guarantees as its evidence grows, while accounting for the adaptive choices made along the way.

For batched queries, the bound's asymptotic data requirements grow with the square root of the number of adaptive questions, retaining the favorable scaling previously available in the static setting. The authors instantiate their result for statistical queries using a clipped Gaussian mechanism. In their empirical evaluation, this approach outperforms baselines assembled from static-data bounds.
neurips-2025-adaptive-data-analysis-for-.tldr: The paper provides generalization guarantees for adaptive analysis that account for growing datasets and adaptively scheduled questions.

paragraphs: Models can predict brain responses from word embeddings or neural-network features without making clear which concepts drive those predictions. The paper identifies superposition as a central obstacle: distinct semantic features become entangled in correlated embedding directions. Different combinations of these directions can then predict identical brain activity, making the fitted weights ambiguous.

The Sparse Concept Encoding Model converts dense embeddings into a larger space of sparse, non-negative concept atoms. Each dimension is intended to represent an interpretable concept, so a voxel's weights can directly express its conceptual selectivity. The change therefore targets the representation used for prediction, making its axes more meaningful for interpreting brain responses.

On fMRI recordings collected during story listening, the model matches conventional dense models in predictive performance while substantially improving interpretability. It supports analyses that separate overlapping cortical representations of time, space, and number, and exposes structured similarities among distributed concept maps. These findings show how preserving predictive ability can coexist with a more interpretable account of conceptual organization.
neurips-2025-disentangling-superposition.tldr: Sparse concept atoms make brain-response prediction weights interpretable while matching dense models on story-listening fMRI data.

paragraphs: Emotion-recognition benchmarks often cover a narrow range of expressions and blur distinctions between related categories. Their images can also obscure faces or represent demographic groups unevenly. EmoNet Face addresses these problems by creating a benchmark designed around detailed emotional categories, visible facial expressions, and controlled demographic coverage.

The suite introduces a taxonomy of 40 categories derived from foundational research. It includes three AI-generated datasets, called EmoNet HQ, Binary, and Big, with full-face expressions and demographic balance across ethnicity, age, and gender. Multiple experts annotate the data, providing material for both training and evaluation. These components make the benchmark's categories, imagery, and evaluation labels part of a coordinated design.

The authors also develop Empathic Insight Face, which reaches human-expert-level performance on this benchmark. That result concerns recognition within the supplied synthetic benchmark, whose controlled expressions are central to its construction. The released taxonomy, datasets, and model give researchers a shared resource for studying finer distinctions in facial emotion recognition.
neurips-2025-emonet-face-an-expert-annot.tldr: EmoNet Face provides expert-annotated synthetic facial-expression datasets covering 40 emotion categories with controlled demographic balance.

paragraphs: Linear temporal-difference learning evaluates a policy using a value estimate built from features. Existing convergence-rate analyses typically require those features to be linearly independent. That requirement excludes many practical representations in which some features overlap or can be expressed through combinations of others.

This paper establishes mean-square convergence rates for linear TD(lambda) with arbitrary features. It obtains these results without modifying the algorithm or adding assumptions to replace feature independence. The guarantees cover both discounted evaluation and the average-reward setting, extending the theoretical treatment across two formulations of policy evaluation.

The central mathematical challenge is that arbitrary features can produce multiple solutions. Instead of requiring convergence toward one particular parameter vector, the authors develop a stochastic-approximation result that measures convergence toward the solution set. This makes the target compatible with non-unique representations. The contribution is therefore a finite-sample account of the existing algorithm's behavior when redundant features prevent the usual single-solution analysis from applying.
neurips-2025-finite-sample-analysis-of-l.tldr: The paper establishes mean-square convergence rates for unmodified linear TD(lambda) with arbitrary, potentially redundant features.

paragraphs: Multimodal language models can struggle with questions whose answers depend on small image details. Cropping can expose those details, but finding a useful crop may require expensive searching or task-specific training. FOCUS uses information already stored inside the model to guide that search without additional training.

The method first identifies the objects mentioned in the question. It then uses the model's key-value cache to construct a map of object relevance across the image. Candidate regions are proposed and ranked using this map, and the highest-ranked crop is used to answer the detailed question. This connects crop selection to the question and the model's internal representation of the image.

Across four fine-grained question-answering datasets and three types of multimodal models, FOCUS reports strong results. It surpasses three popular cropping methods in accuracy and efficiency, and matches the best-performing baseline, ZoomEye, using 3–6.5 times less compute. The findings support informed region selection as a way to preserve detailed visual performance while reducing search cost.
neurips-2025-focus-internal-mllm-represe.tldr: FOCUS uses a multimodal model's internal cache to select useful image crops without training, reducing compute for detailed visual questions.

paragraphs: Efficient 3D-aware head generators often store features on planes and retrieve them using projected coordinates. Conventional Cartesian projections can entangle features and create mirroring artifacts. Spherical planes reduce this entanglement, but uneven mapping from square feature maps wastes representational space and makes fine details harder to generate.

HyPlaneHead introduces a hybrid representation combining planar and spherical components. It also replaces conventional spherical warping with a near-equal-area mapping, improving how much of a square feature map is effectively used during rendering. These changes address both the geometry of feature retrieval and the distribution of representational capacity across the head.

The paper identifies another source of interference: features can penetrate across convolutional channels associated with different planes, especially when one plane dominates. Its generator therefore produces a unified single-channel feature map instead of separate maps in multiple channels. With these improvements together, the authors report state-of-the-art full-head image synthesis, linking the gains to how features are mapped, stored, and kept from interfering.
neurips-2025-hyplanehead-rethinking-tri-.tldr: HyPlaneHead improves full-head synthesis through hybrid feature planes, near-equal-area spherical mapping, and a unified feature map.

paragraphs: Recovering 3D information from video depends on knowing the camera's internal imaging parameters, or intrinsics. Many algorithms treat these parameters as constant throughout a recording, although real-world videos can violate that assumption. Evaluating methods that track changes requires reliable annotations across consecutive frames.

InFlux supplies such annotations for more than 143,000 frames from 386 high-resolution indoor and outdoor videos. The benchmark includes changing intrinsics and broader scene and parameter variation than prior benchmarks. To establish accurate frame-level reference values, the authors build a comprehensive lookup table from calibration experiments and extend the Kalibr toolbox to improve its accuracy and robustness.

Evaluations on InFlux show that most existing baseline methods struggle to predict intrinsics accurately when they change during a video. The benchmark therefore provides both a measurement resource and evidence of a current performance gap. Its consecutive-frame annotations make changes over time directly evaluable, supporting research on camera calibration for videos that depart from the fixed-intrinsics assumption.
neurips-2025-influx-a-benchmark-for-self.tldr: InFlux provides per-frame camera-intrinsics annotations for dynamic videos and reveals substantial difficulties for existing prediction methods.

paragraphs: Recurrent neural networks are used to model brain computation, but they are often trained in supervised, open-loop settings. In a closed loop, the learner interacts with an environment, making that interaction part of the learning problem. This paper develops a mathematical account of how linear recurrent networks learn under those conditions.

The authors show that otherwise identical networks can follow markedly different learning trajectories depending on whether training is open or closed loop. Their analysis separates closed-loop learning into stages associated with changes in training loss. This gives a structured explanation of the divergence rather than treating the environment as an incidental addition to the task.

Two competing objectives govern the closed-loop dynamics: improving the policy in the short term and maintaining stable agent-environment interactions over the long term. The authors also apply the framework to a realistic motor-control task. Together, the results emphasize that interaction and stability matter when using recurrent-network learning as a model of biologically plausible behavior, with the mathematical theory developed for linear networks.
neurips-2025-learning-dynamics-of-rnns-i.tldr: A theory of linear recurrent networks shows how closed-loop learning balances immediate policy improvement against long-term interaction stability.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks differ in their ability to distinguish graph structures. This paper introduces Hierarchical Ego Graph Neural Networks, which use hierarchical node individualization inspired by methods for testing graph isomorphism. The architecture extends subgraph-based networks into a family with progressively greater distinguishing power.

In the limit, the hierarchy can distinguish graphs up to isomorphism: structures that differ only in node naming remain equivalent. The authors also give a precise logical characterization for node classification on graphs of bounded degree. In that setting, the architecture's separating power matches graded hybrid logic, providing a formal language for describing which distinctions it can express.

This characterization supports comparisons with higher-order graph networks, networks augmented with local homomorphism counts, and refinement algorithms based on individualization. Experiments establish practical feasibility and report benefits over traditional graph architectures, both with and without those count features. The paper thus connects an architectural hierarchy to formal expressiveness results while also showing that the proposed models can be used in practice.
neurips-2025-logical-expressiveness-of-g.tldr: HE-GNNs form an increasingly expressive graph-network hierarchy with a logical characterization on bounded-degree graphs and demonstrated practical benefits.

paragraphs: Language-model efficiency can come from reusing parameters or giving different inputs different amounts of computation. Mixture-of-Recursions combines these approaches in one Recursive Transformer. A shared stack of layers is reused across processing rounds, while lightweight routers decide how many rounds each token receives.

At a given recursion depth, attention computation involves only tokens that remain active. The model selectively caches their key-value pairs, improving memory access efficiency alongside adaptive computation. A further variant reuses key-value pairs from the first recursion to reduce memory footprint. These mechanisms coordinate parameter sharing, token routing, and cache management within the same architecture.

Across models ranging from 135 million to 1.7 billion parameters, the authors report improved tradeoffs among model size, predictive performance, and throughput. At equal training computation and smaller model sizes, MoR lowers validation perplexity and improves few-shot accuracy while achieving higher throughput than vanilla and existing recursive baselines. The results support combining repeated use of shared layers with selective computation, rather than treating those efficiency choices separately.
neurips-2025-mixture-of-recursions-learn.tldr: Mixture-of-Recursions combines shared layers with adaptive per-token depth to improve language-model performance and throughput at matched training compute.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can generate samples beyond their training set, but they can also reproduce training examples. This paper creates a mathematically tractable setting for studying the boundary between those behaviors. Its experimental and theoretical laboratory uses fully synthetic data or structured data resembling natural images.

Within that setting, the authors compare the weighted training loss of a fully generalizing model with that of an underparameterized model that memorizes. They characterize a critical level of model parameterization where the generalizing model's loss becomes larger. This crossover provides a concrete theoretical quantity for investigating when training may favor memorization.

Carefully designed experiments show that the predicted crossover locates a transition in diffusion models trained by gradient descent. The theory analytically predicts the model size at which memorization becomes predominant in the studied setting. The contribution is a controlled way to connect a loss-based mathematical comparison with observed training behavior, creating a foundation for further investigations into memorization and generalization relevant to privacy and copyright concerns.
neurips-2025-on-the-edge-of-memorization.tldr: A controlled theoretical and experimental framework predicts when memorization becomes predominant as diffusion-model size changes.

paragraphs: Understanding a region in an image or video involves more than marking its boundaries. Perceive Anything Model combines segmentation with semantic outputs such as object categories, label definitions, functional explanations, and detailed captions. It extends SAM 2 by connecting its visual representations to large language models.

The connecting component, Semantic Perceiver, converts SAM 2 features into multimodal tokens that the language model can interpret. These features already contain information useful for visual recognition, localization, and semantics. The approach uses that existing representation to support several kinds of region-specific output within one efficient framework.

The authors also construct a refined and augmented dataset containing 1.5 million image-region and 0.6 million video-region semantic annotations, including region-level streaming video captions. PAM reports strong performance across diverse region-understanding tasks while running 1.2–2.4 times faster and using less GPU memory than prior approaches. These findings suggest that connecting segmentation features to language generation can support rich regional descriptions without sacrificing the reported computational efficiency.
neurips-2025-perceive-anything-recognize.tldr: PAM connects SAM 2 to language models to segment and describe image or video regions with improved reported speed and memory use.

paragraphs: Models of cellular perturbations aim to predict how single-cell gene-expression profiles respond to changes. PerturBench provides a common framework for developing and comparing these models. It combines a modular evaluation platform, varied perturbation datasets, and metrics intended to reveal different aspects of predictive performance.

The evaluation identifies limitations in widely used models, including mode collapse, where predictions fail to preserve the diversity of responses. It also shows why rank-based metrics matter alongside fit measures such as root mean square error. Evaluating how predictions are ordered supplies complementary evidence about model effectiveness that an overall numerical fit score does not provide alone.

Across the tested datasets and models, no architecture clearly dominates. Simpler architectures are generally competitive and scale well as datasets become larger. These results make evaluation design and straightforward baselines central to assessing progress. The framework is intended to support more reliable model development and the eventual use of predicted cellular responses to simulate genetic and chemical screens for therapeutic discovery.
neurips-2025-perturbench-benchmarking-ma.tldr: PerturBench standardizes cellular-perturbation evaluation and finds competitive simple models, important metric differences, and failures such as mode collapse.

paragraphs: Depth estimated from stereo video needs to remain consistent over time, especially in applications such as augmented reality. Using nearby frames offers limited temporal information, while modeling long-range relationships can be expensive. PPMStereo addresses this tradeoff by maintaining a compact memory of useful frames.

Its Pick-and-Play Memory module divides memory construction and use into two coordinated processes. The pick stage identifies the most relevant frames. The play stage adaptively weights those selected frames when combining spatial and temporal information. This design makes both the contents of memory and their contributions responsive to the information needed for stereo matching.

The purpose of the buffer is to retain informative long-range context without incurring the cost associated with broad temporal aggregation. Experiments report state-of-the-art accuracy and temporal consistency, supporting the effectiveness of the proposed memory construction. The central contribution is a selective way to carry information across video frames, improving the stability of depth estimates while keeping the memory compact and computationally efficient.
neurips-2025-ppmstereo-pick-and-play-mem.tldr: PPMStereo selects and adaptively weights frames in a compact memory buffer to improve stereo depth accuracy and temporal consistency.

paragraphs: This paper studies a privacy mechanism in which a person's data is used in exactly k randomly selected steps out of t possible steps. Such allocation appears in private optimization and aggregation. Existing analyses either produce overly conservative guarantees through shuffling arguments or require Monte Carlo computations that are prohibitive in many practical settings.

The authors provide theoretical guarantees and numerical estimation algorithms specifically for random allocation. Their main comparison bounds its privacy guarantees using independent subsampling, where each step includes the person's data with probability approximately k/t, with the stated asymptotic correction. This links a scheme with a fixed number of participations to a better-understood scheme with independent participation decisions.

Two additional analysis techniques improve the numerical bounds in several parameter regimes. For random allocation with Gaussian noise addition, the combined methods yield efficiently computable, nearly tight results. The practical contribution is more usable privacy accounting for this sampling design, while the theoretical contribution explains how its guarantees relate to those of independent subsampling.
neurips-2025-privacy-amplification-by-ra.tldr: The paper develops efficient, nearly tight privacy bounds for random allocation with Gaussian noise by relating it to independent subsampling.

paragraphs: Combining infrared and visible images requires deciding which information from each source should appear in the result. Existing generative fusion methods can struggle with that balance and with making their information selection interpretable. HCLFuse approaches the problem through a design inspired by human cognitive laws.

Its encoder uses masks at multiple scales and a variational information bottleneck. Posterior probability modeling and information decomposition help extract concise, accurate low-level information from the two modalities. This representation is designed to support detailed structural reconstruction, making information selection an explicit part of the generation pipeline.

HCLFuse also combines diffusion-based generation with physical laws through guidance that changes over time. The guidance adapts to different generation stages, with the stated aims of capturing intrinsic data structure and reducing dependence on data quality. Experiments across multiple datasets report state-of-the-art qualitative and quantitative fusion results, as well as significant improvements in semantic segmentation metrics. The findings connect the method's representation and guidance choices to stronger structural consistency, detail quality, and downstream segmentation.
neurips-2025-revisiting-generative-infra.tldr: HCLFuse combines selective information encoding with time-varying physical guidance to improve infrared-visible fusion and downstream segmentation.

paragraphs: In partially observable reinforcement learning, an agent cannot directly access the full state of its environment. Representing its uncertainty through continuous belief states creates computational challenges. This paper studies an approximation that treats a finite history as a state in a finite-state model called a Superstate MDP.

The authors derive improved guarantees connecting the optimal value of this transformed model to that of the original partially observable problem. They then propose policy-based learning with linear function approximation for the Superstate MDP. The resulting approach uses temporal-difference learning followed by policy optimization, allowing standard MDP-style learning to operate on finite histories.

The analysis shows that approximation error decreases exponentially with history length. It also provides finite-time bounds that explicitly quantify the error from applying standard temporal-difference learning when the true dynamics are not Markovian. This makes the loss from the finite-history approximation part of the learning guarantee, supporting an approximate solution strategy with a characterized relationship between retained history and value accuracy.
neurips-2025-scalable-policy-based-rl-al.tldr: Finite-history states enable approximate POMDP learning with guarantees that quantify non-Markovian error and its exponential decrease with history length.

paragraphs: Large reasoning models often produce long sequential reasoning traces, delaying the final answer. SPRINT aims to shorten the sequential portion by teaching models to identify independent subtasks that can run in parallel. Its framework covers both post-training and execution at inference time.

A data-curation pipeline reorganizes natural-language reasoning into rounds of longer-horizon planning and parallel execution. Fine-tuning on a small amount of this material teaches models to find parallelization opportunities as reasoning unfolds. Interleaving planning with execution allows the model to make those decisions dynamically throughout an extended solution.

In evaluations including mathematics, SPRINT-trained models match reasoning-model performance while generating up to 39% fewer sequential tokens on problems requiring more than 8,000 output tokens. On the out-of-distribution tasks GPQA and Countdown, longer trajectories show reductions of up to 45% and 65% in average sequential tokens while matching the fine-tuned reasoning model's performance. These measurements concern sequential tokens, showing reduced serial reasoning work in the reported settings.
neurips-2025-sprint-enabling-interleaved.tldr: SPRINT teaches reasoning models to interleave planning with parallel subtask execution, reducing sequential tokens while preserving reported task performance.

paragraphs: Graph coarsening reduces a graph's size to save memory and support downstream computation. A reduction matrix maps signals onto the smaller graph, while a lifting matrix maps them back. Most frameworks tie these matrices together as pseudo-inverses and optimize the resulting information loss using Restricted Spectral Approximation, or RSA.

The paper observes that these two matrices have different responsibilities. Constraints on the lifting matrix alone can ensure that important coarse-graph objects, including adjacency matrices and Laplacians, exist. This leaves room to choose reduction matrices more freely. The authors classify admissible families, describe their required properties, and examine whether explicit formulas are available.

For a fixed lifting matrix, changing only the reduction matrix can further decrease RSA. The paper explores examples, including choices obtained through constrained optimization. It also illustrates the effects on node-classification tasks, motivated by the connection between RSA and graph-network performance. The key insight is that an existing coarsening can gain from reconsidering how signals are projected onto it.
neurips-2025-taxonomy-of-reduction-matri.tldr: Allowing reduction matrices beyond pseudo-inverses can decrease signal loss for a fixed graph coarsening.

paragraphs: Coresets reduce training costs by selecting a smaller subset of data, but selection can change the biases a model encounters. This paper investigates how selection affects both spurious correlations within the subset and the robustness of models trained on it. The analysis covers ten benchmarks, five sample-scoring metrics, five selection policies, and multiple subset sizes.

The findings complicate the idea that selecting difficult examples or reducing dataset bias will automatically improve robustness. Embedding-based sample descriptions carry a comparatively lower risk of increasing bias than descriptions based on learning dynamics. However, lower bias in subsets of difficult examples does not reliably translate into robust downstream models.

Very small coresets introduce a particular risk: highly prototypical selections can produce high average performance while concealing weak performance across groups. The results therefore distinguish three properties that can move differently: which examples are selected, how biased the selected dataset is, and how robustly the trained model performs. Average accuracy alone can obscure consequential differences among those outcomes.
neurips-2025-the-impact-of-coreset-selec.tldr: Coreset selection can alter bias and group robustness in different ways, with tiny prototypical subsets sometimes hiding weak group performance.

paragraphs: Noise in scanned point clouds can impair surface reconstruction and shape understanding. Many learned denoisers require paired noisy and clean examples, whose preparation involves substantial manual effort. U-CAN instead learns from multiple noisy observations through a noise-to-noise matching approach, avoiding the requirement for clean training counterparts.

A neural network predicts a multistep denoising path for each point in a shape or scene. A new loss enables statistical reasoning across noisy observations, while an additional constraint encourages consistency in the recovered geometry. These components combine evidence from noisy measurements with a requirement that the denoised output maintain coherent structure.

The authors argue that their consistency constraint is not specific to three-dimensional geometry and can also support image denoising. Evaluations cover point-cloud denoising, upsampling, and two-dimensional image denoising. They report substantial improvements over state-of-the-art unsupervised methods and results comparable to supervised methods. The findings support learning useful denoising behavior from noisy observations when geometry consistency is included in the training objective.
neurips-2025-u-can-unsupervised-point-cl.tldr: U-CAN learns denoising from noisy observations using multistep predictions and consistency constraints, with competitive results across point-cloud and image tasks.

paragraphs: Relationships among variables can change over time, making a single static causal graph an incomplete description of a temporal system. UnCLe addresses this problem by learning time-resolved causal influences from observational time series. Its goal is to capture evolving dependencies in nonlinear systems at scale.

The method pairs Uncoupler and Recoupler networks to separate input series into semantic representations. Autoregressive dependency matrices then model relationships among variables. To estimate dynamic causal influences, UnCLe perturbs the temporal inputs and examines the resulting prediction errors at individual data points. This makes the estimation sensitive to when a relationship affects prediction.

Experiments report better results than state-of-the-art baselines on static causal-discovery benchmarks. They also demonstrate the method's ability to capture evolving temporal causality in synthetic and real-world dynamic systems, including human motion. The distinctive contribution is its representation of changing influences across time, alongside performance on static tasks. Those findings support UnCLe as a promising approach for investigating time-varying mechanisms in complex systems.
neurips-2025-uncle-towards-scalable-dyna.tldr: UnCLe estimates time-varying causal influences using learned temporal dependencies and prediction-error responses to perturbations.

paragraphs: Multimodal reasoning can produce text alone or interleave text with images, and both formats can improve vision-language model performance. This paper investigates what explains those improvements. It proposes visual thoughts as a shared mechanism: expressions that carry image information into the reasoning process.

The authors argue that the benefit depends on how clearly and concisely visual information is expressed, rather than on whether the output format is textual or interleaved. They define four forms of visual-thought expression and analyze their differences. The forms vary in clarity and conciseness, and those differences correspond to different levels of improvement in multimodal reasoning.

The paper also examines the role of visual thoughts inside the transformer. It finds that they act as intermediaries between the input image and reasoning in deeper layers, helping transmit visual information further into processing. This connects an observable property of the reasoning output to an internal information-transfer mechanism. The resulting perspective provides a common basis for understanding improvements across otherwise different multimodal reasoning formats.
neurips-2025-visual-thoughts-a-unified-p.tldr: The paper explains multimodal reasoning gains through visual thoughts that clearly and concisely transmit image information into deeper reasoning.

paragraphs: Streaming speech systems need to begin speaking quickly, but generating the first audio token can create a substantial delay. VITA-Audio addresses both that initial wait and overall generation speed through an end-to-end speech-language model with fast interleaved audio and text generation.

Its lightweight Multiple Cross-modal Token Prediction module generates several audio tokens in one model forward pass. The model can produce audio during its first forward pass, directly addressing the startup bottleneck. A four-stage progressive training strategy supports acceleration with minimal loss of speech quality. The system is trained entirely on open-source data and is described as fully reproducible.

At the seven-billion-parameter scale, experiments report a three- to fivefold inference speedup. The model also significantly outperforms similarly sized open-source models on multiple benchmarks for speech recognition, text-to-speech generation, and spoken question answering. These results combine faster audio production with stronger reported task performance, supporting the approach as a way to make spoken interaction more responsive without treating speed as the sole objective.
neurips-2025-vita-audio-fast-interleaved.tldr: VITA-Audio generates multiple audio tokens per forward pass, reducing startup latency and reporting three- to fivefold faster inference at 7B scale.
